segments: ... they were.
And they also took up trees with the earth of their roots and planted them in the new garden that they dug.
And when evening came,
they had completed the whole work;
and carpets and tapestries were spread,
and all necessary utensils were prepared,
and the Kalatite woman crossed over to it.
And after years, she died.
And great mourning was assumed because of her;
and he ordered, and they demolished that mansion and that garden, and left it desolate.
And he built for her in that place a famous burial chapel,
which until today people of prayer dwell in,
and alms are distributed [there].
After al-Nasir, al-Zahir his son [ruled] for nine months.
During his father's lifetime, they had proclaimed this man heir to the kingdom.
And when al-Nasir his father became afraid of him,
he revoked his proclamation and imprisoned him,
and proclaimed his younger son whose name was Amir Ali.
And Amir Ali died in the days of his father,
and left behind young children.
And his father mourned over him with a great, inexpressible mourning,
even to the point that he sent to all the kings and said to them
that not one of them should send to him an envoy or a letter of condolence.
And he sat alone in a dark house for many days.
And also all the common people of Baghdad took up mourning,
and in every neighborhood a group of women would sit and weep.
And they went about in the markets of Baghdad wearing sackcloth and with their faces blackened,
and wailing as they raised high funeral songs for many days.
And immediately a command went out
that whoever wished to weep,
should weep in her house,
and that they should no longer go outside.
And when Caliph al-Nasir died,
the nobles brought out al-Zahir his son from prison,
because they loved him on account of his goodness;
and they swore [allegiance] to him,
and seated him on the throne of his father.
And as they were seating him, he said:
"How is it fitting for a man to open a shop after the ninth hour? For I have passed fifty years [of age]."
However, when he sat [on the throne],
he showed justice and generosity,
and restored great possessions that had been seized to their owners,
because his father had been very greedy.
And fear was lifted from men,
and slanderers were curbed.
And he built another bridge in Baghdad over the Tigris,
and there were two bridges in it,
because for a period of two hundred years there was only one bridge.
